metadata.title: Claimed authors by chapter, Book of Mormon
metadata.method: Chapter-level attribution based on the text's own claims. Named speakers, record keepers, abridgers, letter writers, divine speakers, and substantial quoted or cited sources are included. Speech and epistles that are only summarized in narration are omitted. Inferred attributions are flagged in chapter notes.

roles.primary author: writes the record or text in his own voice
roles.abridger: Mormon or Moroni condensing an earlier record
roles.source record keeper: author of an earlier record that an abridger used
roles.speaker: delivers a recorded discourse, prophecy, or dialogue
roles.letter writer: author of an epistle or written proclamation whose text is reproduced
roles.divine speaker: the Lord, Jesus Christ, the Father, the Spirit
roles.quoted author: text quoted at length from the brass plates or Bible
roles.cited witness: prophet named as a witness or quoted only briefly
roles.editorial commentator: abridger interrupting with his own commentary

King Benjamin's address begins (chs. 2-5).
Benjamin relays the words of an angel (3:2-27).
This Ammon is a descendant of Zarahemla (7:3), not the son of Mosiah. Limhi questions Ammon (7:9-11) and addresses his people (7:18-33).
Ammon and Limhi discuss the Jaredite plates and seers (8:6-20).

The Record of Zeniff (heading before ch. 9) spans chs. 9-22. Zeniff narrates in first person in chs. 9-10; the record continues in third person under Noah and Limhi and is described as the record kept by Limhi's people (8:5; 22:14).
Abinadi's first prophecy, delivered as the Lord's words ('Thus saith the Lord,' 11:20-25).

Abinadi's second prophecy, again in the Lord's words (12:1-8). Alma the Elder as source for Abinadi's words (chs. 12-17) is inferred from 17:4. A priest quotes Isaiah 52:7-10 (12:20-24); Abinadi begins reciting the commandments given through Moses (12:34-36).
Abinadi continues the Ten Commandments (13:12-24).
Isaiah 53.
Abinadi quotes Isaiah 52:8-10 (15:29-31).
Alma the Elder writes all the words of Abinadi (17:4).
Alma the Elder's teaching at the waters of Mormon. Alma as source is inferred from 17:4 and the heading before ch. 23.
Narrative of Noah's death and Limhi's accession; no speech is recorded at length.

authors.name: King of the Lamanites (in the days of Limhi)

chapters.notes: Limhi questions the captured Lamanite king (20:14, 20:16); the king answers (20:15) and swears an oath of peace (20:24); Gideon counsels Limhi (20:17-22).
Narrated account. Limhi's and Ammon's exchange (21:28) is reported indirectly, so neither is listed as a speaker.
Gideon proposes the plan of escape (22:3-9); Mosiah receives the records kept by the people of Limhi (22:14).
The heading before ch. 23 introduces an account of Alma and his people (chs. 23-24) but does not name a record; Alma the Elder as source is inferred. Alma declines kingship (23:7-14).
The voice of the Lord comes to Alma's people (24:13-14, 24:16) and to Alma (24:23).
Mosiah reads the records to the people, and Alma preaches and baptizes (25:5-18); both are reported in narration, so neither is listed as a speaker.
The voice of the Lord answers Alma (26:15-32); Alma writes the words down (26:33). Alma the Elder as source for the chapter is inferred from 26:33.
The angel rebukes Alma the Younger (27:13-16); Alma relays the Lord's words (27:25).
The Lord answers Mosiah regarding his sons' mission (28:7).
Mosiah's written proclamation to the people (29:5-32; see 29:4).
Alma's record begins (chs. 1-44). Nehor's teaching is summarized in narration (1:3-6), so he is not listed; Alma pronounces judgment on him (1:13-14).
Alma's sermon in Zarahemla.
Alma's sermon in Gideon.
An angel tells Alma to return to Ammonihah (8:15-17); Amulek receives him (8:19-20).
Amulek's address; he recounts the angel's words to him (10:7-8).
Alma questions Zeezrom before healing him (15:6-10); Amulek's actions are narrated only.

The heading before ch. 17 introduces an account of the sons of Mosiah (chs. 17-27) 'according to the record of Alma,' so Alma the Younger remains the source record keeper. The Lord comforts the sons of Mosiah (17:10-11); Ammon answers the Lamanite king (17:23-25).

authors.name: King of the Lamanites (father of Lamoni)

chapters.notes: The voice of the Lord comes to Ammon (20:2); Lamoni's father speaks (20:9-27).
Aaron contends with an Amalekite (21:5-9).

authors.name: King of the Lamanites (father of Lamoni)

chapters.notes: Aaron teaches Lamoni's father.
The king's proclamation is summarized in narration (23:1-3), so he is not listed.
Speech of the Anti-Nephi-Lehi king (24:7-16).
Ammon's rejoicing in the Lord.
The Lord answers Ammon (27:11-12); Ammon reports it to the king (27:13).
Alma's expression of desire.
Korihor's speeches and his written confession (30:52-53).
The Zoramites' Rameumptom prayer (31:15-18); Alma's prayer (31:26-35).
Alma quotes Zenos at length (33:4-11) and Zenock briefly (33:16); Moses and the brazen serpent (33:19).
Amulek's sermon continues Alma's; Zenos, Zenock, and Moses named as witnesses (34:7).
Alma's counsel to Helaman; retells the angel's rebuke (36:8-9, 36:11) and echoes Lehi's words on seeing God upon his throne (36:22; cf. 1 Nephi 1:8).
Alma's counsel to Helaman; Alma quotes the Lord's words concerning Gazelem (37:23).
Alma's counsel to Shiblon.
Alma's counsel to Corianton (chs. 39-42).
Moroni and Zerahemnah negotiate surrender.
The heading before ch. 45 attributes chs. 45-62 to the record of Helaman. Alma blesses and prophesies to Helaman; Helaman takes the records.
Moroni raises the title of liberty and quotes the dying words of Jacob concerning Joseph's coat (46:24-26).
Moroni offers terms to the besieged Lamanites (52:37).
Epistles between Captain Moroni and Ammoron (Moroni 54:5-14; Ammoron 54:16-24).
Moroni's response to Ammoron's epistle (55:1-2); the chapter then narrates the stratagem against the Lamanite guards.
Helaman's epistle to Captain Moroni (chs. 56-58).
Moroni's epistle to Pahoran (59:3) is summarized, not reproduced, so he is not listed as a letter writer.
Captain Moroni's epistle to Pahoran.
Pahoran's reply to Captain Moroni.
62:52 reports Helaman's death, so the closing notice is not Helaman's own writing.

Shiblon takes possession of the records (63:1) and confers them on Helaman, son of Helaman (63:11); 63:17 closes the account of Alma, Helaman, and Shiblon. Shiblon as source record keeper is inferred from his custody of the records; no heading names his record.
The book's heading cites the record of Helaman, son of Helaman, and the records of his sons.
Helaman's death is reported at 3:37; his son Nephi succeeds him. Attribution of chs. 4-16 to Nephi's record is inferred from this succession and the book's heading.

Helaman's counsel to his sons Nephi and Lehi (5:6-12), which they remember (5:5, 5:14); Nephi and Lehi speak from the fire (5:26); the voice above the cloud of darkness (5:29, 5:32); Aminadab speaks (5:41). The second voice (5:46-47) speaks of 'my Well Beloved'; its identification as the Father is inferred.
Nephi names prophets as witnesses of Christ (8:11-22), including Lehi and Nephi, son of Lehi (8:22).
The Lord's promise to Nephi (10:4-11). Nephi's subsequent preaching is narrated, so he is not listed as a speaker.
Mormon's commentary on human frailty. The whole chapter is commentary, so no source record keeper is assigned.
Samuel's prophecy on the wall of Zarahemla (chs. 13-15); Samuel delivers the Lord's words (13:8 ff.) and invokes the angel's message (13:7).
Samuel quotes the angel's charge (14:9) and relays its words (14:26, 14:28).
Samuel cites Zenos on the restoration of the Lamanites (15:11) and quotes the Lord (15:16-17).
The people's response to Samuel is narrated; neither Samuel nor Nephi speaks directly in this chapter.
Nephi, son of Helaman, has departed and left the records to his son Nephi (1:2-3). Nephi, son of Nephi, prays and hears the voice of the Lord announcing the sign of Christ's birth (1:13-14).
Giddianhi's epistle (3:2-10); Lachoneus's proclamation is summarized (3:13-14), and his direct address follows (3:15); Gidgiddoni's counsel (3:21).
Mormon states that he makes his record according to the record of Nephi (5:9-10) and speaks in first person (5:12 ff.). Attribution of chs. 1-28 to Nephi, son of Nephi, follows this statement.
Nephi's ministry is reported (7:15-18) without recorded direct speech.
Mormon's commentary on the preservation of the righteous and the fulfillment of Zenos and Zenock (10:11-19).
Sermon at the temple begins (chs. 12-14, paralleling Matthew 5-7).
Jesus quotes Isaiah 52:8-10 (16:18-20).
Jesus cites Moses (20:23) and quotes Isaiah 52 (20:32-45). Prophecies paralleling Micah 5:8-9 (20:16-17) and Micah 4:12-13 (20:18-19) are noted only; Micah is not named.
Jesus draws on Isaiah 52 (21:8, 21:10, 21:29). A prophecy paralleling Micah 5:8-15 (21:12-18, 21:21) is noted only; Micah is not named.
Isaiah 54.
Jesus commends the words of Isaiah (23:1-3) and asks why Samuel the Lamanite's fulfilled prophecy was not recorded (23:9-13).
Malachi 3; Jesus reports the words the Father gave to Malachi (24:1).
Malachi 4.
Mormon explains that he writes only a part of what Jesus taught (26:6-12).
Mormon's remarks on the Three Nephites (28:17-24, 28:36-40).
Mormon's commentary; no source record keeper is assigned.
Mormon relays the words of Jesus to the Gentiles.
1:1-19 Nephi; 1:19-21 Amos, son of Nephi; 1:21-47 Amos, son of Amos; 1:47-49 Ammaron.
Ammaron instructs Mormon (1:2-4).
The voice of the Lord commands Mormon to cry repentance (3:2) and declares 'Vengeance is mine' (3:15).
Mormon's farewell address to the remnant.
Moroni takes over the record at 8:1.
Moroni's address to those who deny Christ; he quotes Christ's commission to his disciples (9:22-25).
Ether's genealogy (1:6-32); Jared urges his brother to pray (1:34-39); the Lord answers the brother of Jared (1:40-43).
The brother of Jared's plea concerning the barges (2:18-22); the Lord answers (2:20-25). Moroni comments on the decrees of God concerning the land (2:9-12).
The brother of Jared's prayer (3:2-5) and vision of the Lord, who identifies himself as Jesus Christ (3:14). Moroni comments on the vision (3:17-20).
Moroni comments (4:1-5) and relays the Lord's words on sealing the record (4:6-19); the speaker names himself as Jesus Christ (4:7-8).
Moroni's address concerning the witnesses of the plates. The whole chapter is commentary, so no source record keeper is assigned.
Moroni's warning against secret combinations (8:20-26).
Moroni's discourse on faith; the Lord answers Moroni (12:26-28, 12:37).
Moroni summarizes Ether's prophecy of the New Jerusalem (13:1-13) and states that he is forbidden to write more of it.
The epistles exchanged by Coriantumr and Shiz (15:4-5, 15:18) are summarized, not reproduced, so neither is listed as a letter writer. Ether finishes his record (15:33-34).
Moroni relays the words of Christ to the twelve disciples.
Mormon's sermon on faith, hope, and charity (introduced at 7:1).
Mormon's first epistle to Moroni, on infant baptism; Mormon records the words of Christ revealed to him (8:7-8).
Mormon's second epistle to Moroni.
Moroni's farewell and promise concerning the Holy Ghost.
